keys.beat: Antinous rejects Telemachus's charge and blames Penelope for prolonging the courtship.
keys.text: 'It is not the suitors who are to blame, it is your own mother, for she is the most artful woman in the world. This three years past, and close on four, she has been driving us out of our minds.'

keys.beat: He recounts how she wove Laertes's shroud by day and secretly unraveled it by night.
keys.text: 'She set up a great tambour frame in her room, and began to work on an enormous piece of fine needlework. "Sweethearts," said she, "wait till I have completed a pall for the hero Laertes."'

keys.beat: By night she unravelled what she had woven by day.
keys.text: 'This was how she deceived us. She used to keep working at it all day long, but at night she would unpick the stitches again by torchlight.'

keys.beat: A maid exposed the deception and the suitors forced Penelope to finish the web.
keys.text: 'But in the fourth year one of her maids who knew what she was doing told us, and we caught her in the act of undoing her work, so she had to finish it whether she would or no.'

keys.beat: Antinous demands that Telemachus send his mother back to Icarius to choose a husband.
keys.text: 'Send your mother away, and bid her marry the man of her own and of her father's choice... as long as she persists in tormenting us, we will go on eating up your estate.'
